messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: prod-eu-west1 streaming.p99 exceeded 3.2s for the last 5m, > SLO. affected service: inference-runtime-decode, approx 12% of requests saw tail stalls. Grafana -> https://grafana.redwood.local/d/p95/p99-streaming
Aisha (oncall): ack. I'm paged, taking first touch. starting collection: stacks + dmesg + kernel logs on a few affected hosts.
Riley (sre): I see correlated pagefault noise on hosts gw-eu-02 and gw-eu-04, pmap evictions spiking. Could be compilepath change from last night's rollout.
Marco (runtime): we rolled a new kernel-compilepath patch 00:30 UTC that includes a new TRT8/flashattn binding and a small linker tweak + -fno-strict-aliasing flag for decode perf. Reverting that is our first hypothesis.
Aisha (oncall): good context. Riley, can you snapshot /proc/zoneinfo and vmstat and attach? Marco, can you identify the exact kernel package sha?
Riley (sre): attached snippets: (truncated) vmstat shows rate of pgmajfaults rising ~2.5x. proc/zoneinfo shows high DMA/Movable free fragmentation on those hosts.
Marco (runtime): kernel package: build-2026.03.14-kp-7f3b9 -> commit 7f3b9b2. It was part of the TRT8 driver rollout. I have the deploy job ID: deploy/rollout/2026-03-14-21: deploy-bot should have logs.
deploy-bot: rollout deploy/rollout/2026-03-14-21 completed to 60% at 01:02 UTC, rollout paused on anomaly at 01:18 UTC. See CI job -> https://ci.redwood.local/job/rollout/2026-03-14-21
Olga (platform): to reduce customer impact we should route traffic away from gw-eu-02/04 and spin up fallback nodes with previous kernel. Can we do immediate traffic shaping?
Aisha (oncall): yes. Riley, please cordon gw-eu-02 and gw-eu-04 from LB rotation and drain. Use quick command: kubectl -n infra annotate node gw-eu-02 maintenance=true && kubectl drain gw-eu-02 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
Riley (sre): running drain now. draining gw-eu-02 -> 5 pods, gw-eu-04 -> 4 pods. Starting fallback instances with kernel build-2026.03.10-kp-61.
Marco (runtime): I'll prepare a rollback artifact for kernel build-2026.03.10-kp-61 and coordinate hotpatch. Quick mitigation: disable the new linker opt by env flag in runtime: RUNTIME_LINKER_OPT=off, that reduces the path that touches the new TRT bindings.
Aisha (oncall): do it. Riley, after draining confirm p99 trends stabilize. Nikhil, notify support/CS: customers may see degraded streaming for ~20-30m and we'll provide status.
Nikhil (support): pinged #support with preliminary advisory. Marking impacted customers: enterprise accounts with long-lived streams in EU region. Creating ticket CS-18922.
Marco (runtime): pushed env change to canary nodes: RUNTIME_LINKER_OPT=off. Command used: kubectl -n runtime set env deploy/inference-runtime RUNTIME_LINKER_OPT=off --record
Aisha (oncall): checking metrics... p95 improved almost immediately, p99 dropping from 3.4s -> 1.1s on canary. Good sign.
Riley (sre): hosts drained and fallback nodes online. p99 across eu-west1 trending down but still noisy on a few racks. Investigating kernel slab activity and mm reclaim thresholds.
Marco (runtime): I pulled dmesg from gw-eu-04 before drain: repetitive stack traces in kernel module flashattn_bind: WARN_ON_ONCE slab object leak signaled, and later page_alloc failures. Suspect flashattn binding path triggers less-friendly allocation pattern under streaming workloads.
Olga (platform): topology note: gw-eu-02/04 are on older NIC microcode which plus the new kernel path may aggravate page coloring. We'll keep them out of rotation until we can validate.
Aisha (oncall): escalation: Marco, please open an incident ticket with runtime team and attach repro steps and kernel logs. Also we need an emergency rollback plan if env toggles don't fully resolve.
Marco (runtime): creating runtime-issue #INC-7041 with logs, commit refs, and suggested rollback to 2026.03.10 build. Add repro harness: run streaming stress with seq_len=1024 and concurrency=16. Example load command: 
```
wrk -t8 -c200 -d120s http://inference-eu-west.local/stream -s scripts/stream_stress.lua --seq 1024 --concurrency 16
```
Aisha (oncall): good. Also let's capture a heap profile from one of the affected nodes before full reboot to help kernel/repro. Riley?
Riley (sre): saved /var/log/kern.log and perf samples. Uploading to incident storage -> s3://incidents/6387654321/trace.tar.gz.
Nikhil (support): CS update: posted to impacted customers that we're mitigating with node reroute and will follow up with root cause in the next update.
Marco (runtime): quick note: if rollback needed, we can cut a staged kernel rollforward in 3 waves: canary (10%), partial (40%), full. we should keep canary for 10-15m to ensure p99 stable before full.
Aisha (oncall): agreed. Timeline: +10m check canary metrics, +30m decide rollback. If p99 < 1.5s and pgmajfaults return to baseline we close oncall. Otherwise roll back.
Olga (platform): coordinating infra: we have capacity to run rollback parallel on 6 hosts in eu-west. Will prepare kernel bundle and pre-seed packages to avoid node boot lag.
Riley (sre): noting customer-impact: estimated total requests affected ~18k during spike window, peak error injection low but streaming stalls caused session resets for long-lived streams.
Aisha (oncall): closing loop: after env toggle + draining + fallback nodes, p99 is stable at ~0.9s for 15m. Keeping this thread open for RCA. I'll handoff to Marco for root cause follow-up.
Marco (runtime): taking ownership for RCA and follow-up. Next steps: reproduce, bisect kernel change (flashattn binding + linker tweak) and if confirmed issue, revert kernel patch and push a hardened test in CI for streaming workloads.
Nikhil (support): will craft customer-facing RCA once runtime provides root cause and mitigation timeline.
Aisha (oncall): thanks everyone. If anything regresses, re-alert and mention this thread. I'll update incident tracker: INC-7041 -> status: mitigated, monitoring.
deploy-bot: done: rollback plan doc added to incident INC-7041 -> https://wiki.redwood.local/incidents/INC-7041
